Strategy: Take the lower-quartile bin. Prefer the bin ranking one quarter up among all open bins, counting residuals below it, tight but skipping the very tightest bins and ignoring loose outliers. This keeps the tightest for exact fits and the loosest for big items, so ranking can differ from Best Fit whenever the quartile bin is not the tightest. It may help by filling tight representative bins, but may fail by stranding the tightest bins if later items run large.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    n = len(bins)
    return [-abs(sum([1 for s in bins if s < r]) - (n - 1) / 4) for r in bins]
```
generator_note: Lower-quartile rank targeting: prefer bin whose residual rank is closest to (n-1)/4.
